alternatives.root_cause: ad was redeployed with a broken artifact and fails on request handling
alternatives.why_not: A bad artifact usually shows as crashloops or startup failure affecting all traffic, and nothing in the blast radius points at a release; a flag flip explains an empty change log.

alternatives.root_cause: ad exhausted heap/thread capacity and began rejecting requests
alternatives.why_not: Exhaustion typically ramps with rising latency and caller timeouts before hard errors, and would not single out ad at an instantaneous onset.

verdict.summary: A feature flag toggled in flagd enabled the failing ad-service code path, causing ad to return errors on a large share of requests.
verdict.reasoning: Only ad alerts, and the blast radius is exactly ad plus its flag source (flagd) and its callers upstream (frontend, frontend-proxy) - that is error propagation toward the caller, not a shared-dependency outage. flagd's other consumers (cart, recommendation, product-reviews, fraud-detection) are healthy, so flagd itself is fine; what differs is the flag value ad evaluates. An error rate that appears instantly with no downstream service degraded and no artifact change fits a runtime flag flip on an ad-specific code path (the familiar adServiceFailure-style toggle) better than a deploy or resource problem. If ad were merely slow rather than erroring, dependency_latency would fit, but the alert is error rate.
